title: Silicon anode swelling and fracture
bottleneck: Silicon stores ten times more lithium than graphite but swells about 300 percent on lithiation, pulverizing particles and continuously cracking the solid-electrolyte interphase. Each crack exposes fresh silicon that consumes lithium and electrolyte, so capacity fades within hundreds of cycles. Nanostructuring and yolk-shell designs contain the swelling in the lab but add cost and cut volumetric energy density.
why_it_blocks: Silicon anodes are the nearest-term path to higher EV range without new cathode chemistry. Swelling-limited lifetime keeps commercial cells at low silicon blends of 5-10 percent, leaving most of the theoretical gain unrealized.
current_state: Blended silicon-graphite anodes are now common in premium EVs, and pre-lithiation plus advanced binders have pushed cycle life higher. But a pure-silicon anode with automotive lifetime at competitive cost remains unsolved, and solid-state designs face the same expansion stresses.
